We model the SE using a two-coronae framework, in which a warm, optically thick corona (WC) produces the optical/UV and soft X-ray emission, while a hot, optically thin corona produces the hard X-ray continuum. We also test a hybrid model that adds relativistic reflection. The optical/UV coverage constrains the Comptonization seed photon temperature to 0.1-5.5 eV. The two-coronae model consistently describes the broadband emission, with WC electron temperatures kT_e ~ 0.1-0.9 keV and photon indices $Γ> 2$, consistent with previous studies. However, 9/21 AGN require the hybrid model, suggesting that the SE has multiple origins whose relative contributions vary. This is especially evident in UFO hosts, where 4/7 observations favor the hybrid model. Compared with sources without UFOs, UFO hosts show lower WC temperatures, harder hot-corona spectra, and positive hardness ratios. These trends should be treated cautiously because of the small sample and their dependence on spectral parameters and instrumental response. We find no significant differences between AGN with and without WAs. Our correlation analysis finds links between the amplification factor and WC temperature, WC optical depth and hardness ratio, and WC slope and optical depth with UV luminosity. We also find a tentative anticorrelation between WC optical depth and UFO outflow velocity.

papers.title: Tidal Disruption Events in Active Galactic Nuclei: Thermal Radiation and Jets
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, dozens of Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) have been identified, with many more expected from upcoming surveys. A small subset has been observed to launch transient, highly luminous relativistic jets, for which the origin of the requisite magnetic flux has not been identified. A non-negligible fraction of TDEs are expected in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs), where a magnetized accretion flow is already present. As shown first by Chan et al. (2019), the collision of a TDE debris stream with this flow can substantially alter both disk and debris dynamics, leading to a possibly Eddington-limited flare. Here, we use the Athena++ radiation magnetohydrodynamic (RMHD) code to simulate the time near peak fallback rate of a TDE in an AGN, studying the debris-disk interaction, the radiation emitted, and the accumulation of magnetic flux near the horizon. In the example simulated, the accretion rate climbs to $\sim 12\,\dot{M}_{ \rm Edd}$, while the escaping solid angle-integrated luminosity approaches $\sim L_{ \rm Edd}$. The photon luminosity is strongly asymmetric, brighter in the hemisphere from which the debris strikes the disk and dimmer in the hemisphere toward which the debris travels. The photon spectrum peaks in the EUV. The polar magnetic flux grows $\sim 33$-fold, enough to raise the Blandford--Znajek luminosity by a factor $\sim 10^3$, reaching a level sufficient to power observed TDE jets. The polar magnetic flux is also asymmetric, likely making any jet similarly asymmetric, but in the opposite sense to the photon flux.

papers.title: Clumpy Outflows from Super-Eddington Accreting Black Holes. II. Conditions for Clump Formation
papers.abstract: Active galactic nuclei (AGNs) commonly exhibit ultra-fast outflows (UFOs) with velocities of $0.03$--$0.3~c$. Recent high-resolution X-ray observations with XRISM/Resolve suggest that UFOs may have a clumpy structure. However, the formation and evolution of these clumpy outflows remain poorly understood. In the first paper of this series, we investigated the formation of clumpy outflows using numerical simulations and find that sufficiently high spatial resolution is required to reproduce clumpy structures numerically. In this second paper, we perform a series of numerical experiments to identify the key physical processes governing clump formation. We find that spatial fluctuations of physical quantities at the disk surface are essential for the formation of clumpy outflows, whereas spatial and temporal fluctuations at the inner boundary have only a minor effect. Furthermore, density structure-function analysis suggests that the high-density regions have an elongated morphology with characteristic transverse widths of several tens of $R_{\rm g}$, possibly produced by radiation Rayleigh--Taylor instability. A more comprehensive investigation of the instability in general-relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations, where accretion disk structures emerge self-consistently, is expected to provide deeper insights into the physical origin of clumpy outflows.

papers.title: Static tidal Love numbers of Schwarzschild and non-Schwarzschild black holes in quadratic gravity
papers.abstract: We calculate the static electric quadrupolar response of black holes in four-dimensional quadratic gravity, with action $R-αC^2+βR^2$. The Schwarzschild solution has zero massless gravitational Love number under the stated boundary conditions. A numerical non-Schwarzschild solution instead has a nonzero negative response. At $α/r_h^2=1/2$, we find $λ_E/r_h^5\simeq-0.1224928$ and $k_2^{(r_h)}\simeq-0.1837391$, with a final outer-endpoint change in $k_2^{(r_h)}$ of about $1.60\times10^{-7}$. We explain how the background is obtained by shooting and how the tidal solution is selected by matching at an intermediate radius. The perturbations are written in Kodama--Ishibashi gauge-invariant variables. After the scalar-curvature perturbation is excluded by horizon regularity and the absence of an applied scalar tide, the remaining static sector has three coupled second-order radial equations. We define the curvature amplitudes in these equations and describe why simple attempts to separate them fail. The coupling scan shows a negative response approaching zero near the Schwarzschild intersection. We also explain why this full-theory result does not conflict with the removal of curvature-squared operators in a perturbative low-energy expansion.

papers.title: Models of spectral bumps of primary cosmic rays and multi-messenger tests
papers.abstract: The energy spectra of individual species of cosmic ray nuclei by recent direct detection experiments show complicated structures with spectral hardenings and softenings rather than featureless power laws, which challenge the traditional understanding of the production, acceleration, and propagation of cosmic rays. Particularly, the DAMPE measurements reveal charge-dependent softenings and reject mass-dependent softenings with a high significance. Taking into account the correlated structures at similar energies in the large-scale anisotropies of cosmic rays, one of the most natural interpretations of the spectral structures is the presence of a nearby cosmic ray source. In this case, the softening energies correspond to the acceleration upper limits of such a source, forming the so-called Peters cycle of the spectra. Alternative models such as the injection/acceleration and propagation models may also reproduce the spectral bumps, but show difficulty to explain the anisotropies. Fluxes of secondary nuclei and $γ$ rays offer additional tests of different models. Future multi-messenger observations are expected to be able to pin down the origin of cosmic rays.

papers.title: Spiraling into the `snail' cluster MCXC J0157.4-0550
papers.abstract: We present a deep Chandra (130 ks) study of a striking, tidally induced cold front in a subcluster merging with the galaxy cluster MCXC J0157.4-0550. The subcluster, nicknamed the `snail' (J0157), displays an extensive spiral structure that extends to $\sim 260$ kpc --- one of the largest spiral cold fronts identified to date. Surface brightness and spectral analysis across four sectors reveal a consistent density jump of a factor of $\sim 3$ across the front, together with significant temperature discontinuities, and thermodynamic mapping further delineates the coherent, low-entropy structure of the stripped gas. Unlike classical sloshing cold fronts, the spiral in J0157 arises not from oscillation of a displaced cool core, but from subcluster gas that has been ram pressure stripped and tidally wound into a spiral by orbital rotation. Applying Gaussian Gradient Magnitude filtering and azimuthal surface-brightness analysis, we identify quasi-periodic corrugations along the front consistent with candidate Kelvin-Helmholtz (KH) instabilities, with a characteristic scale of $\sim 90$ kpc. The presence of these KH rolls constrains the effective ICM viscosity to $\lesssim 0.59$ times the Spitzer value and the magnetic field strength at the interface to $\lesssim 5.9\ μ$G. These results establish J0157 as a useful laboratory for probing macro-scale merger-induced gas dynamics and micro-scale plasma transport processes in the intracluster medium.

papers.title: Adaptive Model-Switch Thermodynamic Integration: A Bayes Factor Estimator
papers.abstract: Bayes factors are a widely used model comparison criterion, but are often quite challenging and computationally expensive to estimate well. We propose a variation of the model-switch thermodynamic integration method for estimating Bayes factors that decreases the variance of the estimator and essentially eliminates integration error. We choose samples whose density in $β$ is proportional to the standard deviation of previously drawn samples. Rather than averaging many samples at each $β$, we use a very dense set of $β$ values, collecting one sample at each in order of increasing $β$ and one sample at each in order of decreasing $β$ to minimize "thermic lag". We study our procedure with a toy model (based loosely on some signal recovery problems). In this model we find that adaptive sampling gives us a 2.7-fold decrease in the spread of the estimated Bayes factor. We test our procedure both drawing directly from the posterior distribution and using a Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampler.

papers.title: Modeling Multi-band Active Galactic Nuclei Lightcurves Using an Self-supervised Attentive Neural Process Network
papers.abstract: With the the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), observations of tens of millions of quasars are expected. We present a machine-learning framework based on an attentive neural process (ANP) that models stochastic quasar variability and jointly performs two tasks: (i) probabilistic reconstruction of quasar light curves in all six LSST bands, and (ii) inference of physical parameters of the AGN system --- black hole mass, Eddington ratio, and intrinsic variability timescale --- with joint, full-covariance posteriors. The model processes all six bands within a single masked attention mechanism, so that observations in any band constrain the shared driving process, and natively handles irregularly and asynchronously sampled light curves with realistic heteroscedastic noise. We train and evaluate on full ten-year light curves simulated with a relativistic accretion-disk reprocessing model, observed through the fielded Rubin baseline cadence with per-visit photometric noise. The light-curve model is trained with self-supervised, learning from the sparse noisy observations alone and never accessing the underlying noiseless light curves. On a held-out test set, we show that our ANP model reach comparable performances to that of the near-optimal baseline Gaussian process model, while exceeding it in power spectrum reconstruction and damped-random walk timescale estimation. The compact learned latent representation supports future downstream applications, and the fully observation-driven training objective enables direct fine-tuning on real LSST light curves.

papers.title: The evolution of 3C 306 in the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622: linking spectral ageing, ICM conditions, and jet dynamics through MHD simulations
papers.abstract: We present a methodology for analysing radio sources in galaxy clusters by combining multi-frequency radio observations, X-ray analysis of the intracluster medium (ICM), and three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations, and apply it to the galaxy cluster RXCJ1454.4+1622 and its associated FR II radio galaxy 3C 306 (IC 4516). The radio emission exhibits a curved structure connecting the lobes, likely indicating a complex dynamical evolution influenced by environmental effects. Spectral index and break-frequency maps reveal a relatively homogeneous radiative ageing distribution, with characteristic spectral ages of $\sim220$ Myr and a smooth spatial gradient. From equipartition arguments, we estimate an equivalent jet magnetic field of $2.1 \pm 0.3\,μ$G, consistent with values observed in FR II radio galaxies. These observational constraints are used to initialise non-relativistic MHD simulations exploring three scenarios: jet precession, bulk motion of the source through the ICM, and a combined model including both effects. Neither pure precession nor pure source motion alone fully reproduces the observed morphology, whereas the combined model provides a more consistent representation of the jet curvature and lobe asymmetries. Nevertheless, the simulations indicate that source motion is the dominant mechanism shaping the large-scale radio morphology, with jet precession playing a secondary role. The inferred source velocity ($\sim280$ km s$^{-1}$) and precession timescale ($\sim250$ Myr) are compatible with the spectral ageing constraints. These results suggest that the morphology of 3C 306 is influenced by the interplay between jet precession and dynamical interaction with the ICM, highlighting the role of environmental effects in radio-galaxy evolution in clusters.

papers.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
papers.abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.

papers.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
papers.abstract: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. A component correlated with a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) annihilation template remains with finer spatial binning and the instrumental response included. Outside the Fermi bubbles footprint, it is detected at nominal significances of about 4-16$σ$ over 5.6-130 GeV, falling to 1-7$σ$ when the enlarged boundaries of a recent substructured bubbles model are also excluded. With the substructured model, which improves the fit substantially, the component remains at 7-18$σ$ in four of six representative foreground configurations. However, its amplitude and spectrum depend strongly on the foreground model, and no tested foreground yields a single NFW normalization across the sky, including with additional spatial freedom in the eROSITA bubbles. Simulations show that foreground mismodeling can produce spurious NFW-correlated emission of the observed amplitude, and that residual-derived bubbles templates can bias the recovered spectrum. The 420 GeV $W^+W^-$ spectrum motivated by the LZ connection describes the data for some foreground models but is disfavored by others. These results disfavor interpreting the full excess as annihilation in a smooth NFW halo and weaken the case for a common origin with the LZ event, but they do not exclude a dark matter contribution to the persistent halo-like residual. [abridged]

papers.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
papers.abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. We point out a distinct coherent channel when the baryonic component that stores the condensate is superfluid: an effective beta-conversion event between a neutron condensate and normal protons can proceed as an Andreev process, converting a particle-like excitation into a hole-like excitation while adding or removing a Cooper pair from the condensate. The resulting Andreev contribution to beta equilibration is fourth order in the effective conversion vertex, is enhanced by anomalous neutron Green's functions, and is not captured by standard Urca process. We identify the density, temperature, and oscillation-frequency regimes where this channel can dominate viscous damping of neutron-star oscillations and mergers.

papers.title: ExHaLe-jet: Modeling blazar jets with an extended hadro-leptonic radiation code
papers.abstract: Blazars - active galaxies with the jet pointing at Earth - emit across all electromagnetic wavelengths. As the one-zone model becomes increasingly inadequate to describe blazar emission, more elaborate models are needed. In order to self-consistently describe the entire electromagnetic spectrum, extended jet models are necessary. Notably, kinetic descriptions of extended jets can provide the temporal and spatial evolution of the particle species and the full electromagnetic output. ExHaLe-jet is a lepto-hadronic, extended-jet code allowing for in-depth studies of the particle and radiation evolution on all scales. Here, we present our ongoing study regarding acceleration scenarios of particles within the large-scale jet structure. A single acceleration of particles at the jet base (or elsewhere) is insufficient to produce sufficient photon flux. Thus, re-acceleration through, e.g., consecutive shocks along the jet is needed. We explore two possible scenarios for this.

papers.title: SN 2025wiu: A Type Ib Supernova with Post-Peak Optical Rebrightening
papers.abstract: We present optical photometric and optical/near-infrared spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a Type Ib supernova (SN) at z = 0.046927. The r-band light curve exhibits an initial maximum of approximately -18.2 mag, followed by a weaker optical rebrightening reaching approximately -17.8 mag at +38 days in the rest frame relative to the first maximum. However, the reconstructed bolometric light curve does not show a distinct second peak, but instead exhibits a reduced decline rate during the corresponding phase. The spectra consistently show Type Ib features without narrow emission components associated with circumstellar material. The late-time bolometric decline rate of 0.054 +/- 0.008 mag/day is faster than expected for complete trapping of 56Co decay. A radioactive-decay model for the first peak requires nickel mass = 0.47 solar masses, above the range typical of SNe Ib. A combined radioactive-decay and circumstellar-interaction model reproduces the full bolometric light curve with nickel mass ~ 0.38 solar masses, ejecta mass ~ 4.7 solar masses, and an effective circumstellar mass of ~ 0.10 solar masses, with the interaction contributing from the first peak onward. The lack of interaction signatures in the spectra favours an aspherical, disk-like circumstellar structure engulfed by the ejecta, in which the interaction energy is thermalized below the ejecta photosphere; the fitted circumstellar parameters are therefore effective values rather than direct measurements of the circumstellar geometry. SN 2025wiu demonstrates that optical rebrightening does not necessarily imply a genuine bolometric secondary maximum and highlights the importance of multi-band observations for identifying the powering mechanisms of double-peaked stripped-envelope supernovae.

papers.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
papers.abstract: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.

papers.title: Exploring Cosmic Rays from Gravity-Limited Acceleration at Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: We show that horizon-scale magnetic fields around supermassive black holes (SMBHs), only limited by gravity, yield a universal, model-independent ceiling on electromagnetic energy density. For rotating SMBHs, this field enables particle acceleration up to $\sim\!10^{27}$\,eV set solely by fundamental constants. We identify a parameter space in accretion rate and magnetic field strength in which quiescent nuclei simultaneously satisfy the transparency conditions for Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECR) escape and the field requirements for reaching Ultra-High Energies (UHE), naturally complementing photon-rich Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), which favor neutrino production but suppress UHECR escape. We observe that, when including curvature energy losses, the energy of the primaries scales weakly as $E_{\rm curv}\!\propto\!M^{1/4}$ and allows to achieve UHE across different compositions and SMBHs masses ($10^6$--$10^{10}\,M_\odot$), without requiring extreme spins or super-Eddington accretion. A cross-correlation of the Pierre Auger Observatory (PAO) public data with galaxies hosting reliably measured SMBH masses, separating AGN from quiescent hosts, reveals marginal local excesses ($\lesssim\!2.8σ$) consistent with isotropy after correcting for the look-elsewhere effect. The framework provides a direct link between black-hole physics and the maximum energies of cosmic particles, and defines concrete observational tests for next-generation UHECR datasets.

papers.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
papers.abstract: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. By examining past glitches from the ATNF catalog, we quantify the double-detectability prospects of current- and next-generation GW detector networks. We further explore what astrophysical constraints could be placed following a double non-detection using extrapolations from the 2024 Vela pulsar glitch as a stand-in example. We find that a network with at least one next-generation detector greatly increases the probability of double-detection for many known glitching pulsars and improves the detection threshold in glitch energy by nearly two orders of magnitude over existing LIGO detectors. Additionally, double non-detections with networks with at least one next-generation detector could place dramatically improved limits on properties of the pulsar.

papers.title: Three-dimensional spatial modelling of nuclear de-excitation lines
papers.abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants, but interstellar ionization rates suggest an additional low-energy cosmic-ray (LECR) component. LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV gamma-ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can constrain the LECR flux, morphology, and acceleration mechanisms. We construct all-sky maps of Galactic de-excitation emission using three-dimensional (3D) CR distribution models. By comparing them with the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, we assess the detectability of the de-excitation line components against the underlying continuum. We calculate the emission by combining 3D CR distributions from GALPROP and gamma-ray production cross sections from TALYS. We also model an additional LECR component motivated by the high ionization rates measured in the ISM. The predicted de-excitation emission is relatively weak when integrated over the broad regions commonly adopted in MeV gamma-ray analyses ($|l|\leq30^{\circ}$ and $|b|\leq15^{\circ}$), contributing only $\lesssim 1\%$ above the leptonic continuum even considering the additional LECR component. The all-sky maps reveal that, in the standard scenario, the de-excitation-to-leptonic flux ratio remains low over the entire sky, reaching at most ${\sim}20\%$ toward the Galactic anticenter. In contrast, models including an additional LECR component exhibit a pronounced enhancement toward the GC, where the ratio exceeds $100\%$, indicating favourable prospects for detection through spatially resolved analyses. The 6.1-to-4.4 MeV intensity ratio is particularly sensitive to the maximum energy of the injected LECR spectrum, varying by up to ${\sim} 30\%$. Future MeV gamma-ray observatories could thus identify a distinct LECR population and constrain its acceleration and transport.

papers.title: A blazar is a blazar is a blazar ... Comparing long-term varaibility properties of PKS 1510-089 and PKS 2155-304
papers.abstract: Blazars are typically divided by spectral appearance; may that be strength of optical emission lines or the frequency of the synchrotron peak. However, this may say nothing about the variability properties of the various types. Here, we study the long-term variability properties with nearly 20 years of multiwavelength data of one flat-spectrum radio quasar, PKS 1510-089, and one high-frequency-peaked BL Lac object, PKS 2155-304. Both exhibit strong variability with an energy-dependent variability amplitude. Using the total data sets, we do not find any correlation between the various bands. While the flux distributions of PKS 2155-304 are compatible with log-normal functions, this is not the case for PKS 1510-089. We conclude that the one-zone model is inadequate to describe the long-term evolution of blazars, requiring multi-zone or stratified models. Nevertheless, the underlying jet physics appear similar between the two types and in both sources the variability is, in fact, variable.

papers.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
papers.abstract: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source towards M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multi-mission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at $L_{0.5-8.0\rm~keV}\sim10^{38}-10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few $10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of $\sim0.5$ day ($\sim$6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and non-flare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the non-flare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate mass donor at a persistently high rate with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically-regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.

papers.title: Ranking Prompt--Plateau Correlations in Gamma-Ray Bursts with Symbolic Regression
papers.abstract: Gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations probe central engines, relativistic outflows, and radiation processes. The Dainotti relation is an anticorrelation between the X-ray plateau luminosity $L_a$ and rest-frame plateau duration $T_a^{\rm rest}$. We use symbolic regression to compare it with other low-dimensional correlations in 251 GRBs with Swift-XRT plateau properties and Swift-BAT prompt-emission parameters. We perform a Dainotti-guided search, in which $\log T_a^{\rm rest}$ is always present, and an unrestricted search over subsets of at most three variables. The guided search recovers the Dainotti dependence; a D'Agostini fit gives $\log L_a=(51.92\pm0.30)-(1.31\pm0.09)\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with intrinsic scatter $σ_{\rm int}=0.82\pm0.05$ dex. In the unrestricted ranking of 377 feature subsets, the classical Dainotti relation remains competitive, within the top $\sim25\%$ of the tested search spaces. The highest-ranked screened expression is $\log L_a\approx0.855\log L_{\rm peak}-0.782\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with RMSE $\approx0.46$ and $R^2\approx0.88$. The highest-ranked runs repeatedly reduce to this prompt--plateau structure, without retaining additional spectral, absorption, or afterglow-shape variables. A direct regression gives $\log L_a=4.718+0.776\log L_{\rm peak}-0.805\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with $R_{\rm P}=0.91$ for 246 bursts. An errors-in-variables refit gives consistent coefficients. After removing shared luminosity-distance dependence, the relation retains non-negligible explanatory power ($R^2\approx0.62$), consistent with a possible intrinsic component. Restricted Monte Carlo null tests give $p\approx0.01$. Plateau luminosity therefore shows a coupled dependence on prompt luminosity and plateau duration.

papers.title: Seeing Through the RFI Mask: DT-FISTA Inpainting of Pulsar Dynamic Spectra via Fourier Sparsity
papers.abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) frequently contaminates radio observations, and excising affected samples leaves masked regions in sampled images. Replacing masked samples with zero or the mean causes spectral leakage in Fourier-domain power representations. This contamination is particularly severe for modern pulsar scintillation studies, which rely on identifying and characterizing faint parabolic scintillation arcs in secondary spectra, the 2D power spectra of dynamic spectra. Scintillation arcs probe discrete scattering screens in the interstellar medium (ISM) and constrain their physical properties. However, leakage can obscure faint arcs whose power is often $<10^{-3}$ of the dominant pulsar signal power. Wiener inpainting can mitigate this leakage, but a dense implementation requires $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ memory and $\mathcal{O}(JN^2)$ time for $N$ pixels and $J$ iterations, which is computationally expensive for full-resolution spectra containing millions of pixels. We introduce the decreasing-threshold fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (DT-FISTA). Using a sparse Fourier representation, DT-FISTA initially estimates masked intensities from the strongest Fourier components and progressively refines them with weaker components as the soft threshold decreases. Nesterov momentum extrapolation accelerates these updates. Each iteration uses 2D fast Fourier transforms (FFT) and pointwise operations, requiring $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory. Tests on $300\times300$ pixel patches from Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) observations yield lower reconstruction errors than the dense Wiener implementation, with runtime and memory requirements reduced by factors $>10^3$. Applied to full-resolution dynamic spectra, DT-FISTA suppresses mask-induced artifacts and reveals previously obscured faint arcs, enabling efficient ISM studies.

papers.title: Maximal efficiency of geometric beaming and polarization of highly super-Eddington X-ray sources
papers.abstract: Geometric beaming is an often invoked explanation for the apparent super-Eddington luminosities of ultraluminous X-ray sources. It is a natural consequence of the geometrically thick envelope that is expected to surround the inner accretion disk in the super-Eddington accretion regime; as the radiation can only freely escape through a narrow funnel-shaped cavity, the flux along the funnel axis is enhanced. A fraction of the photons will nevertheless escape the funnel cavity at larger angles, reducing the effectiveness of the beaming. To explore the limits of geometric beaming, we performed Monte Carlo simulations of conservative radiative transfer in an infinitely optically thick funnel while accounting for polarization. We discovered that the beaming becomes inefficient when the funnel opening angle is small $(\lesssim15^\circ$) because the photons tend to remain trapped within the cavity until they reach the upper edge of the funnel where they can escape at larger angles. For most of the photons to escape a narrow funnel through a small solid angle, the funnel has to be unrealistically long. Consequently, geometric beaming could at most boost the apparent luminosity by a factor of a few dozen in our idealized simulations. While larger boost factors on the order of $\sim$100 are possible for funnels with a length of $\gtrsim10^5$ Schwarzschild radii, this requires very narrow opening angles of $\lesssim3^\circ$. Additionally, we found that aberration due to mildly relativistic velocities does not significantly change this result. The maximal polarization degree of light reflected by the funnel remained on the order of a few percent for face-on sources and $\lesssim10\%$ for edge-on sources.

papers.title: What can a uniform reflection pipeline establish about supermassive black hole spin? An audit and a corrected analysis of 57 AGN with XMM and NuSTAR
papers.abstract: We audit an automated relativistic-reflection pipeline that fitted one XMM-Newton EPIC-pn and NuSTAR epoch for each of 57 AGN with relxillCp+xillverCp, and repeat the analysis with its failures corrected. The pipeline's apparent constraints were not controlled: Small Window pn backgrounds were never subtracted, the nearest-in-time pairing selected mismatched or nearly empty spectra, single-start fits often stopped short of the minimum, and most fits were inadequate or at a parameter limit. The corrected analysis uses in-window backgrounds, 41 sources with eligible pn--NuSTAR pairs, multi-start fits, bidirectional profiles, criteria fixed in advance and eight model variations. 24 of the 41 reference fits have $p\ge0.01$ and 18 pass all quality checks. Their 90% spin sets comprise 1 two-sided interval (NGC 4051, $0.46\le a_*\le0.93$), 6 lower bounds, 4 upper bounds, 4 disconnected sets and 3 unconstrained profiles. For 10 of the 18 the best fit lies at $i\ge75^\circ$, implausible for type-1 AGN, and most of those constraints disappear when $i\le60^\circ$ is imposed. Only 2 of the 15 constrained sets keep their type both under that limit and with pn restricted to 3--10 keV (an upper bound for Mrk 1040 and a weak lower bound for 1H 0419-577). Simulations show that, with a correct model, the 90% sets contain the true spin in 82--92% of cases without drifting edge-on, but at high inclination one low-spin simulation in six yields a false lower bound. We make no statement about the spin distribution or a spin--jet relation.

papers.title: Gamma-ray calorimetry of Seyfert winds
papers.abstract: Two stacking analyses with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) detected GeV emission from radio-quiet Seyferts, one selected by an X-ray ultra-fast outflow (UFO) and one hard-X-ray-bright, with similar luminosities attributed to different mechanisms: wind shocks and the accretion-disk corona. We investigate how efficiently Seyfert outflows convert mechanical power into GeV photons, whether the two detections require distinct mechanisms, and how Seyferts compare with low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). Without new Fermi-LAT data reduction, we homogenize published measurements to 0.1-100 GeV, place local mechanical accelerators on one L_gamma-Edot diagram, and express eta = L_gamma/Edot as a fraction rho of the complete-calorimetry efficiency eta_max ~ 2.5%, inverting rho for the ambient density required by pp losses. Winds from Seyfert active galactic nuclei (AGN) have rho = 0.020 (+0.018/-0.011) for acceleration efficiency 0.1, a factor of ~13.5 below starburst superwinds (rho = 0.26 (+0.37/-0.16)). The difference exceeds a factor of three with probability 0.95 and is independent of acceleration parameters common to both classes; it is conditional on the wind kinetic powers, collapsing only if every wind sits at its minimum launch radius. The implied densities, ~10 and ~100 cm^-3, are consistency values: density, shock radius and speed are degenerate. The two stacking detections agree within a factor of 1.75 in gamma-ray output per unit Eddington luminosity, but the 95% interval, 0.26-24, is too wide to distinguish them. A third stack, of 186 low-luminosity AGN, extends the comparison 1.5 dex lower, ordered by AGN power. GeV detectability of non-jetted AGN is set by the product of mechanical power and calorimetric fraction. LINER outflows fail on power; for the adopted wind energetics, Seyfert UFO winds fail on calorimetry; starburst superwinds succeed on both.

papers.title: $\texttt{GASTRO-BH}$: Effects of a Central Black Hole in GSE-like Dwarf-galaxy Mergers Around Milky Way-like Hosts
papers.abstract: Recent evidence points to an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) in the most massive globular cluster of the Milky Way, $ω$ Centauri. This globular cluster is commonly associated with the Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy, the last major merger event of our Galaxy, as its nuclear star cluster remnant. Motivated by this, we investigate whether the interaction between a bright GSE-like dwarf galaxy with stellar mass in the range $10^{8.5}$--$10^{9.7}$ solar masses and a Milky Way-like host can either suppress or enhance the growth of a central black hole (BH) during the merger process. To this end, we perform high-resolution $N$-body and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations with the ChaNGa framework and a modified, angular-momentum-aware Bondi-Hoyle accretion prescription, considering both isolated dwarf galaxies and merger simulations with different stellar feedback efficiencies. The merger simulations show that the interaction does not halt BH accretion; instead, tidal interactions and gas inflows during pericentric passages strongly enhance accretion, leading to BH mass growth by more than two orders of magnitude in both low- and high-feedback models. The enhanced accretion is accompanied by suppressed star formation in the dwarf galaxy. Our results suggest that mergers similar to the GSE event can efficiently fuel IMBH growth in satellite galaxies rather than suppress it. This may be in tension with the estimated low mass of the proposed IMBH in $ω$ Centauri, but it could provide a mechanism for triggering active galactic nucleus activity in dwarf galaxies.

papers.title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
papers.abstract: The standard magnetic braking (MB) model has long failed to explain key properties of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs)---including their accretion rates, the formation of ultracompact binaries, and orbital expansion---casting doubt on binary evolution and gravitational-wave progenitor predictions. Phenomenological modifications exist, but a unified, physically grounded mechanism has been missing. Here we show that the overlooked coupling between magnetic saturation and irradiation-driven winds (IDW) provides this missing framework. Accretion-powered irradiation enhances the donor wind, which in turn amplifies MB exactly where needed. Our Saturated MB + IDW (SMB+IDW) model simultaneously resolves three outstanding discrepancies with no fine-tuning: (1) it reproduces the full observed distribution of accretion rates across persistent and transient LMXBs; (2) it naturally explains ultracompact X-ray binary formation; and (3) it quantitatively matches the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries---a critical independent test failed by all previous models. Critically, the SMB+IDW model transforms MB from an externally imposed condition into a self-consistently regulated process tied to the accretion history. By unifying LMXB evolution to MSPs in a single physical picture, our work resolves the long-standing diversity puzzle and establishes a physics-based foundation for next-generation population synthesis, gravitational-wave progenitor predictions, and compact binary interpretation across cosmic time.

papers.title: A Multiwavelength View of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5: an X-ray Luminous and Eclipsing Dwarf Nova
papers.abstract: We report the independent discovery of the cataclysmic variable (CV) SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 using Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey 12 band photometry, following its initial identification via ASAS-SN variability. Here, we investigate the system using optical photometry alongside optical and X-ray spectroscopy. High-cadence optical light curves from publicly available TESS data and a dedicated campaign at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in Brazil revealed a highly inclined system exhibiting pronounced eclipses with an orbital period of 1.81 hours. We found no evidence of a WD spin period. Despite seasonal gaps, the long-term ASAS-SN light curve revealed several outbursts (15 with $Δ$mag $\sim$ 1.5 brighter than the mean magnitude) and one superoutburst over the past decade. During Swift X-ray telescope observations, the system exhibited X-ray luminosity of $8.5 \times 10^{31}$ erg s$^{-1}$ in the 0.3-10\,keV band, originating from thermal plasma emission at a temperature consistent with accretion shocks. Optical spectroscopy from the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrographs on the Gemini South telescope confirms the CV nature of the system, showing strong, double-peaked H and HeI emission lines alongside a weak HeII4686 line. Altogether, these features strongly support the classification of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 as a quiescent, eclipsing dwarf nova with an unusually high X-ray luminosity.

papers.title: A New AI/ML Based Image Reconstruction Technique for Hard X-ray Coded Aperture Imagers
papers.abstract: Here we demonstrate a new AI/ML based image reconstruction method for coded-aperture instruments that provides a pathway for embedded real-time use on-board spaceflight missions. Using the Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) for our initial simulated demonstration, we used our new technique to replace the standard Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) based image reconstruction pipeline. In our alternative approach, we have created a neural network that maps detector counts directly to source positions using simulated responses from selected Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) observations. The network combines convolutional feature extraction with attention and is trained at around 900 source counts. Under zero background noise, it achieves over 93\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with 400 detected source photons. The model maintains at least 90\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with up to 8{,}500 added background counts for sources with 900 detected photons. Within the evaluated region of BAT's field of view, these results show that source position can be recovered from sparse coded-aperture measurements in a wide-field instrument. A key feature of this technique is that explicit inclusion of the mask pattern is not required. This allows us to train the algorithm to "see" using data accumulated from an imaging system. These new non-traditional imaging techniques show substantial promise in enabling efficient imaging using non-planar geometries, which will enable new classes of hard X/$γ$-ray imaging systems and simultaneously improve imaging capability for currently operating instruments.

papers.title: The transformative power of ALMA2040 for mm-VLBI
papers.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has resolved horizon-scale emission in M87* and Sgr A*. Extending these observations to fainter black holes, multiple frequencies, and evolving structures requires greater sensitivity and new observing capabilities. We investigate how ALMA2040 could expand the scientific reach of global millimeter very long baseline interferometry (mm-VLBI), compared with ALMA's Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU). Phasing a larger ALMA array and enabling simultaneous observations across multiple ALMA bands would improve sensitivity and frequency phase transfer, providing spectral and polarimetric diagnostics of gravity, accretion flows, magnetic fields, and relativistic jets. In the configurations studied, ALMA2040 achieves sub-mJy baseline sensitivity at 230 GHz and improves prospects for faint-source imaging at 345 GHz, opening a path from individual horizon-scale targets toward population studies. Simulated observations of M87* show improved multi-frequency recovery of emission from the compact ring-like region toward the jet base, enabling studies of the accretion-jet connection. For Sgr A*, simulations of interstellar scattering mitigation yield a 27% reduction in the error of the recovered intrinsic source structure relative to the WSU configuration. Beyond black holes, these capabilities benefit geometric-distance measurements, stellar masers, compact transients, and other applications of high-resolution astrophysics. Together with rapid-response capabilities across the VLBI network, ALMA2040 could support a transition from isolated snapshots toward multi-frequency, time-resolved studies of compact sources.

papers.title: Sparking Dynamic, Relativistic Magnetic Reconnection in a Twisted Flux Tube
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection around neutron stars (NSs) forms small-scale currents while transferring energy to electron-positron pairs. These dissipating currents cover a wide range of scales, potentially leaving an imprint on time-variable X-ray bursts and pulsed radio emission. We present a reduced, planar model of internal reconnection in a magnetic flux tube with relativistic magnetization, finite resistivity, and strong guide field. Comparing with realistic NS parameters, this model represents the dynamics of a slender magnetic flux tube that is much thinner than the stellar radius. The seed current profile is smooth and does not spontaneously reconnect; instead, a discrete and localized current perturbation is introduced, representing e.g. localized energy release from a NS crust or magnetosphere. Three high-resolution relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulations are described: one has uniform resistivity and Lundquist number such that reconnection proceeds in the plasmoid-mediated regime; the other two account for the feedback of charge starvation on the resistivity in current layers, where density is depleted; we provide a more general explanation for this depletion. All simulations produce a few dominant magnetic X-points and a secondary Kelvin-Helmholtz instability that excites high-wavenumber currents. We quantify the reconnection rate, the intermittency of dissipation, and the time profile of current spikes. We further present three-dimensional simulations confirming a limited growth of the ideal kink mode in the strong guide field regime. Applications are discussed, including to radio pulse microstructure and current damping below the magnetar surface during an X-ray flare, leading to mass loss and X-ray afterglow.

papers.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
papers.abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.

papers.title: Four Which I Knew Not: The Hexadecapole Nearly Cancels the Octupole in Librating Kozai-Lidov Cycles
papers.abstract: Phenomena requiring close proximity between two bodies, from black-hole mergers to hot Jupiters, may originate in hierarchical triples, in which secular torques from a distant companion drive the inner binary's eccentricity nearly to unity. Population syntheses of these channels commonly integrate the double-averaged (DA) secular equations truncated at octupole order. We show that, for a fixed outer orbit, this truncation fails for the slow evolution on librating Kozai-Lidov cycles, in which the argument of pericenter librates. On these cycles the leading octupole kicks to $j_z$, the component of the inner angular momentum along the outer one, cancel pairwise, and the hexadecapole enters at the order of the surviving octupole torque, with the opposite sign. Strikingly, as the inner mass ratio vanishes the two nearly cancel, and their sum changes sign within the librating window, so octupole-truncated integrations omit part of the leading slow torque on this class. For $|j_z|\ll1$, the slow dynamics driven by the hexadecapole is approximately solved analytically as a simple pendulum in the doubled azimuth of the eccentricity vector, with closed-form coefficients on rotating and librating cycles. For a circular outer orbit the hexadecapole-modified cycles are solved exactly. For unequal inner masses the octupole adds to the pendulum's torque on librating cycles, where its alternating kick can also flip orbits, and generally dominates rotating ones. DA integrations follow the predicted excursions, periods and flip criteria. Population consequences depend on the validity of the high-eccentricity reduction and on other processes affecting the cycles.

papers.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: X-ray point sources towards the giant radio lobes of Centaurus A
papers.abstract: Centaurus A (NGC 5128) is the nearest radio galaxy (d = 3.8 Mpc), so individual X-ray point sources can be resolved against its giant radio lobes. We test whether a compact X-ray source population over the lobes exceeds the expected field population, once the selection function, foreground stars and the cosmic X-ray background (CXB) are accounted for. From five Chandra/ACIS-I lobe pointings we build a 0.5-7 keV catalogue of 185 sources, with Bayesian hardness ratios, Gaia DR3 and AllWISE counterparts, and spectral fits to the eight brightest. The hardness-ratio distribution (median -0.17; 80% of sources below N_H = 10^22 cm^-2) is that of background AGN plus a few foreground stars. Above the flux at which half the footprint is covered, the good sample holds 83 sources, 9 of them foreground stars, against 101 expected background sources: 27% below the expectation (-1.5 sigma including a 15% normalisation uncertainty), with no excess. The 90% upper limit on a lobe-associated excess above 6.9x10^36 erg/s is N_lobe < 18, or < 38 for a conservative 30% normalisation uncertainty. With the usual resolved-source masking and CXB subtraction, no additional lobe-associated correction to diffuse-emission or inverse-Compton measurements is indicated.

papers.title: Are $E>B$ regions essential for particle injection in relativistic magnetic reconnection?
papers.abstract: During relativistic magnetic reconnection, X-points ($E>B$ regions at vanishing guide field) have been proposed to play an essential role in injecting particles into the nonthermal population. Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations at a range of magnetizations $σ\equiv B_0^2/(4πn_0 m_e c^2) = 12$--$800$, we study in detail how the particle energy gains up to the injection threshold $γ_{\rm inj} = σ/4$ are partitioned into work done inside $E>B$ regions (unmagnetized), within one gyration after exit (re-magnetizing), and at all other times (magnetized). The magnetized channel supplies the largest part of the energy gain for $\sim 95\%$ of injected tracers at $σ= 12$ and $\sim 65\%$ at $σ= 800$. Most of the tracers in this magnetized majority never enter an $E>B$ region before injection. We also compare these injection shares with the earlier studies that proposed an essential role for $E>B$ regions. We conclude that $E>B$ regions are neither necessary for injection nor the dominant direct contributors to pre-injection work by injection share in two-dimensional, nonradiative pair-plasma reconnection at vanishing guide field.

papers.title: Breakdown of hydrodynamic universality in causal first-order viscous neutron star oscillations
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic modeling of viscous neutron stars requires a choice of theory of relativistic hydrodynamics. That distinct formulations contain the same physical content in the long-wavelength limit is referred to as ``hydrodynamic universality.'' It has been recently shown that hydrodynamic universality can break down in radial neutron star oscillations: causality and finite-size effects restrict access to the long-wavelength universal hydrodynamic regime in sufficiently viscous stars. We show that this breakdown occurs for a broad range of causal hydrodynamic frames in Bemfica--Disconzi--Noronha--Kovtun (BDNK) theory. Increasing viscosity collectively pushes this class of causal frames away from the BDNK regime of validity, eventually forcing all to lie outside it at bulk viscosities in the range $ζ\sim10^{30}$--$10^{31}\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. This breakdown of universality is accompanied by material changes in the oscillation mode structure: non-hydrodynamic modes become damped on timescales comparable to those of hydrodynamic modes, the first overtone can become longer lived than the fundamental mode, and unphysical instabilities with sub-millisecond timescales can emerge. Even in regimes where universality has broken down, we find that the inviscid threshold of gravitational collapse remains unchanged in BDNK theory. These results provide evidence that first-order theories of relativistic hydrodynamics may be insufficient for modeling sufficiently viscous neutron stars.

papers.title: Convective Oscillations of Cosmic Rays
papers.abstract: Turbulent motion of the background plasma can introduce fluctuations in the spatial distribution of cosmic rays (CRs). For an ensemble-averaged Gaussian CR distribution with a width $ Λ\left( t,p \right) $ at time $ t $ and momentum $ p $, it is found that $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) $, the fluctuation power spectra induced by incompressible and acoustic turbulent convection, respectively, have power-law asymptotics in wavenumber $ k $: $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^4 $ and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^2 $ for $ k\ll 1/Λ\left( t,p \right) $; $ P_\text{s}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{γ_\text{s}-4} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{s} $, and $ P_\text{d}\left( t,k,p \right) \propto k^{γ_\text{d}-2} $ for $ k\gg 1/L_\text{d} $, where $ γ_\text{s} $ and $ γ_\text{d} $ are the spectral indices of the velocity power spectra of the incompressible and acoustic turbulence below their outer scales $ L_\text{s} $ and $ L_\text{d} $, respectively. These results have implications for probing interstellar turbulence via future high-resolution images of pulsar gamma-ray halos.

papers.title: Secular Evolution of Quasiperiodic Eruptions: eRO-QPE2
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) are recurrent soft X-ray flares from galactic nuclei. In this work, we analyze both the quiescent and eruption emission of eRO-QPE2, using 11 XMM-Newton observations spanning $4.33\,{\rm yr}$. The key findings include (1) the eruption peak count rate remains approximately constant, while the quiescent count rate shows an approximately linear decline superposed with a large-amplitude oscillation; (2) no secondary eruptions are detected between the normal eruptions and any such events would have to be fainter by more than two orders of magnitude; (3) the recurrence time decreases at an average rate of $\dot{T}_{\rm rec}\approx-5\times10^{-6}$. These findings are consistent with an extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) interacting with a precessing accretion disk and producing two normal eruptions per orbital period. Bayesian timing analyses further constrain the EMRI orbital eccentricity to $e<0.033$ (at $95\%$ confidence level).

papers.title: Extracting the Central Sound Speed of Neutron Stars through Intrinsic Stellar Structure Scaling with Reduced Equation-of-State Model Dependence
papers.abstract: Inferring neutron star (NS) core properties remains sensitive to the assumed equation of state (EOS). Using a nonlinear Walecka model with generalized $ω$-meson self-interactions, we construct six EOS families, each containing $10^3$ samples subject to identical nuclear and astrophysical constraints. Despite satisfying these constraints, the families predict markedly different high-density behavior and core properties; higher-order $ω$ interactions can also generate interior sound-speed peaks within purely nucleonic matter. To reduce this model dependence, we use the intrinsic and perturbative analysis of the dimensionless Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations (IPAD-TOV) to derive an EOS-independent estimator $Θ(\rm{X},Ψ)$ of the central squared sound speed $s_{\rm c}^2$, where $\rm{X}=P_{\rm c}/\varepsilon_{\rm c}$ is the central EOS-parameter and $Ψ$ characterizes the stellar-mass response to central energy density. For canonical $1.4\,M_\odot$ NSs, $Θ$ correlates linearly with $s_{\rm c}^2$ across the families ($R^2\approx0.94$-$0.99$). The family-dependent relations converge toward a common optimum: minimizing their dispersion yields $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.523\pm0.044$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.173^{+0.020}_{-0.018}$ for all six families, or $s_{\rm c}^2\approx 0.496\pm0.092$ and $\rm{X}\approx 0.167^{+0.030}_{-0.029}$ when the family without $ω$ self-interaction is excluded. The corresponding radii are $11.73^{+1.08}_{-0.92}$ and $11.92^{+1.76}_{-1.28}\,\rm km$, respectively, with $95\%$ confidence intervals. A unified scaling fitted to all EOS samples supports both extractions. These results show how common stellar-structure relations can constrain NS core properties with reduced EOS-model dependence, even when existing observations cannot distinguish among the underlying EOS descriptions.

papers.title: Probing fundamental physics with ALMA2040 mm-wavelength observations of neutron stars
papers.abstract: Bursty or (rotation-induced) pulsed coherent radio emission from pulsars, magnetars, and fast radio transients originates in some of the most extreme environments in the Universe. However, the exact physical mechanism behind the scenes remains poorly understood. ALMA2040 will allow for systematic exploration of the millimeter-wavelength spectral window for pulsars and fast radio transients for the very first time, offering unprecedented opportunities to discover new observational phenomena and advance our understanding of emission physics. Beyond this, ALMA2040 provides a unique means to unveil the neutron-star population in the Galactic Centre (GC), enable novel tests of fundamental physics in the vicinity of the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, probe the potential existence of dark matter in the GC, and investigate the dense, highly dynamic interstellar and magnetic environment of this region.

papers.title: A Shell Collision Scenario for EP251222b/GRB 251222A: Connecting Prompt Emission and Double-Peaked Afterglow
papers.abstract: GRB 251222A is a long-duration gamma-ray burst at a spectroscopic redshift of $z=3.171$. It was detected by the EP as the soft X-ray transient EP251222b before and during the gamma-ray emission. We performed a multi-wavelength (EP/WXT, fermi/GBM, swift/XRT and optical/NIR) investigation of this event. Its prompt soft X-ray and gamma-ray features, together with two afterglow rebrightenings, allow us to examine a possible connection between the prompt ejecta and the afterglow. We consider a multiple-shell scenario in which a faster, narrower shell catches up with a slower, wider shell. We assume that the selected pulse groups trace different ejecta and that the late X-ray flare marks their collision. Under these assumptions, we represent the post-collision outflow by an effective merged core and an outer annular component. A joint fit to the multi-band afterglow gives a Lorentz factor of $Γ_c\approx293$ for the merged core and $Γ_{1,w}\approx228$ for the outer component. The sample-wise collision mapping gives an energy release of $E_{\rm diss}=(1.6^{+2.1}_{-0.9})\times10^{52}$ erg and a dynamical dissipation efficiency of $0.37^{+0.07}_{-0.14}\%$. EP251222b can therefore be used to test a prompt--afterglow connection through shell collisions, although it does not uniquely establish this interpretation.

papers.title: Numerical simulations of low-mass black hole-neutron star mergers with moderate eccentricities
papers.abstract: A confident detection of orbital eccentricity in gravitational-wave signals from black hole-neutron star systems would be a strong indicator of their dynamical formation origin. While eccentric waveform models have recently been developed, their validity for analyzing black hole--neutron star signals has yet to be tested against numerical-relativity simulations. Building upon our previous study of quasicircular black hole--neutron star mergers, we perform simulations of a subset of these systems with orbital eccentricities around five times larger than those inferred for GW200105_162426. Additionally, we perform simulations with magnetized matter to assess whether trapped $g$-mode oscillations persist in strongly magnetized disks. Regarding the emitted gravitational-wave signal, we find that the effective one-body waveform model SEOBNRv5EHM shows reasonable agreement unless tidal contributions become important, and the inspiral-only post-Newtonian models pyEFPE/pyEFPEHM show larger disagreement in the late inspiral. For the equal-mass system, which has the largest effective tidal deformability, eccentric tidal corrections have a small but noticeable impact on the phase, $\sim0.1$ rad. We find an almost negligible impact of eccentricity on the properties of the remnant black hole, and differences of up to a factor of two in the remnant disk mass. Trapped $g$ modes in the accretion disks have the same frequency regardless of the eccentricity, confirming that they depend mainly on the properties of the remnant black hole. We find that when accretion disks are strongly magnetized, they become less dense and have less pronounced structure, and that the trapped $g$ modes previously identified in the unmagnetized cases are efficiently damped.

papers.title: Polarization Properties of Thomson-Scattering Triaxial Ellipsoids
papers.abstract: Polarimetry is a powerful tool for constraining the geometry of distant astrophysical objects. Continuum polarization induced by Thomson scattering can probe the photospheric geometry of transients and provide insight into their explosion mechanisms. We systematically study continuum polarization from spheroids over a broader range of deformations and viewing angles than considered previously, and generalize the calculation to triaxial ellipsoids. We find that strongly deformed spheroids exhibit a non-monotonic dependence of polarization on viewing angle, a behavior overlooked in previous studies. Triaxial ellipsoids show more diverse polarization signatures, but their qualitative behavior can be understood from the area of surface elements viewed nearly edge-on, where the local polarization is strongest. Our results provide a simple physical understanding of the dependence of polarization on photospheric geometry and help constrain the geometry of astrophysical transients through polarimetric observations. The computational results of this study will be made publicly available for use in future research.

papers.title: Identification of ultra-high-energy neutrinos in vertical air showers with surface detectors
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential of surface detector arrays to identify ultra-high-energy neutrinos using vertical air showers with zenith angle $θ\leq 60^\circ$, a region largely unexplored in current searches. The method exploits the enhanced electromagnetic component at ground level arising from energetic leptons produced in neutrino interactions. Using detailed air-shower and detector simulations, we show that observables sensitive to the electromagnetic and muonic content provide genuine discrimination between neutrino-induced and hadron-induced showers. This is demonstrated both with idealized shower quantities and with realistic detector-level signals based on water-Cherenkov and scintillator detectors. The corresponding neutrino identification efficiency is used to derive the effective mass and, primarily, the effective area of the array under background-rejection requirements appropriate to targeted multi-messenger searches. Although not competitive with inclined-shower searches under the stringent background rejection factors required for diffuse-flux analyses, this approach establishes the feasibility of a vertical detection channel, extending the field of view of surface arrays and providing a complementary tool for multi-messenger observations of transient sources.

papers.title: Optical observations of supernova candidates with the ILMT
papers.abstract: The International Liquid Mirror Telescope (ILMT) is a 4-m optical ({\em gri} spectral bands) zenithal survey telescope with a field of view of 22.3$\times$22.3 arcmin, suitable for discovery and follow-up of faint transients. With the \texttt{PyLMT} pipeline, several new transients, including supernova candidates, are being discovered and detected routinely. We report the discovery of six supernova candidates, AT~2023yjc, AT~2024agkc, AT~2024aifv, AT~2024aiha, AT~2024fxn, and AT~2024zsm, using the ILMT. Ten additional supernova candidates were discovered in other surveys but were also detected with the ILMT. Here, we present the light curves of all supernova candidates observed with the ILMT in the {\em gri} bands. The basic light curve parameters, such as the rise time, decline rate, and peak magnitude, are estimated and reported.

papers.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
papers.abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.

papers.title: Neutrino production at the extreme vicinity of supermassive black hole in NGC 1068
papers.abstract: The identification of NGC~1068 as an extragalactic high-energy neutrino source raises the question of the physical conditions required for neutrino production. Motivated by the newly updated IceCube data (down to $\sim 0.2 \,\rm TeV$) for NGC 1068, we present a statistical, model-independent inference primarily constrained by the multi-messenger observations. We calculate neutrino production from hadronic channels (including hadronuclear and photomeson processes) and the accompanying cascade gamma rays, and then employ the Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) method to explore the parameter space comprehensively, constrained by observational data. According to our results, the emission region is tightly limited: $R \gtrsim 10\,R_{\rm s}$ is excluded at $\sim 5σ$, and $R \gtrsim 6\,R_{\rm s}$ at $\sim 3σ$, where $R_{\rm s}$ is Schwarzschild radius of supermassive black hole (SMBH). Furthermore, reproducing $\gtrsim 80\%$ of the observed neutrino flux further restricts the emission to $R \lesssim 3R_{\rm s}$. Finally, we explore the possible particle acceleration mechanisms and find that stochastic acceleration naturally satisfies all constraints, whereas alternative mechanisms require extreme, fine-tuning parameters. We therefore identify stochastic acceleration as the most viable origin of the neutrino emission from NGC~1068.

papers.title: Detecting and Identifying Supernovae in AGN Accretion Disks
papers.abstract: Stars may become embedded in active galactic nucleus (AGN) accretion disks and eventually explode as supernovae (SNe), whose detection would provide direct evidence for the existence and evolution of stars in AGN disks. We investigate the electromagnetic emission of such disk SNe using an analytic shock dynamics model coupled with a one-zone radiation model. Applying this framework to four progenitor types over a range of AGN black hole masses and Eddington ratios, we find that disk SNe around lower-mass black holes (BHs) or at lower Eddington ratios are more readily detectable against the underlying AGN emission and can remain detectable over a broader range of electromagnetic bands, from the infrared to soft X-rays. However, detectability against the AGN background does not guarantee that disk SNe can be distinguished from isolated SNe with CSM interaction. We therefore further compare disk SNe with isolated SNe with and without CSM interaction and find substantial degeneracies in their macroscopic observables. Nevertheless, we identify distinctive signatures that are robust across progenitor types. The characteristic emission shifts from the EUV for \(M_{\rm BH}\lesssim10^7\,M_\odot\) toward the UV/optical for \(M_{\rm BH}=10^8\,M_\odot\), with the visibility timescale increasing from less than a day to \(\sim3\text{--}70\) days and \(T_{\rm peak}\sim3\text{--}8\) eV in the latter case. The UV/optical regime around \(10^8\,M_\odot\) BHs therefore offers particularly promising prospects for detecting disk SNe.

papers.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
papers.abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and dlog-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlator, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a user-friendly Mathematica package MadStree for computing arbitrary tree-level cosmological correlators.

papers.title: Isospin breaking in $ρππ$ couplings: $ρ^{+,0}$ width difference and muon $g-2$
papers.abstract: The dominant contribution to the hadronic vaccum polarization (HVP) of the muon $g-2$ can be calculated using the hadronic spectrum in $τ^- \to π^-π^0ν_τ$ decay, provided isospin breaking (IB) corrections are properly accounted for. Among these corrections, IB in the $ρππ$ coupling has been pointed out as a missing ingredient. In this work, we calculate this IB effect within the impulse approximation using a symmetry-preserving framework based on Dyson-Schwinger and Bethe-Salpeter equations, incorporating fully dressed quark propagators and meson Bethe-Salpeter amplitudes. We then estimate its effect in the HVP contribution to the muon $g-2$. As a natural extension, we also compute the IB in the ratio of $φK^+K^-/φK^0\bar{K^0}$ couplings and compare with existing data. We obtain a coupling ratio $g_{ρ^0π^+π^-}/g_{ρ^+π^+π^0} = 1.0024(17)(1)$, which yields an isospin-breaking correction of $Δa_μ^{\mathrm{HVP,LO}}[ρππ] = -2.32(1.64)\times 10^{-10}$ to the two-pion contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment extracted from $τ$ decay data.

papers.title: Blueprint for an AI-Enabled Particle Theory Community
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in the capabilities and reach of artificial intelligence (AI) are changing research in particle physics. In this new era, AI is an innovative tool for theoretical physicists, while the interaction of AI and particle theory is itself a developing field. We argue that particle theory requires a community-scale effort to realize its full potential. We show how particle theory occupies a unique position in the AI for physics landscape, and describe the complementarity of AI and theory developments. We conclude with a series of recommendations on how to build an AI-enabled theory community for the Genesis Mission.

papers.title: Magnetic-field dependence of the QCD electric screening mass parameter through $g^4$ in hot and dense matter
papers.abstract: A constant magnetic field modifies the hard electric screening sector of hot and dense QCD and generates a directional splitting at $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$. We determine the strict-hard screening pole through $g^4$ for three massless flavors with physical $u,d,s$ charges, retaining the full $eB/T^2$ dependence without a weak- or strong-field expansion. The shifted-frequency construction used for the two-loop exchange contribution is a background-field Feynman-gauge curvature; we derive and apply its local conversion to the ordinary Feynman-gauge self-energy before assembling the screening pole. The leading magnetic shift is isotropic, while the $g^4$ directional splitting arises from the one-loop anisotropic kinetic normalization; the symmetry-allowed finite-density $A_0F_{12}$ mixing is numerically small over the studied range for physical $u,d,s$ charges. For $μ/T=0$ and $1$, the magnetic $g^4$ coefficient is positive over $0\le eB/T^2\le4$ and is strongly reduced by density. Extending the calculation to $0\leμ/T\le2$ at $eB/T^2=1$ and $4$ reveals sign reversals of both the leading magnetic coefficient and the directional splitting at sufficiently large density. The zero-field limit reproduces the Braaten-Nieto result and its finite-density extension by Vuorinen. The running coupling used only for the phenomenological magnetic mass shift is chosen independently of $B$, so that all magnetic-field dependence through $g^4$ resides in the calculated coefficients.

papers.title: Four-loop electron EDM matching and timelike $τ$ electric dipole form factor
papers.abstract: We compute the four-loop matching of a CP-odd four-$τ$ interaction onto the electron electric dipole moment (EDM), together with the leading timelike $τ$ dipole form factor generated by the same source. Both results are scale independent at this order. Without a local electron dipole, exact electron-EDM cancellation still leaves a timelike $τ$ signal proportional to the four-$τ$ coefficient.
